Lets callers that surface exception text to logs or users see why an I/O failure actually happened, not just a fixed generic string.

result.summary: This PR captures errno and folds SysErrorString() into the exception messages thrown by AutoFile::write(), write_buffer(), read() (via detail_fread), ignore(), and BufferedFile::Fill() when they hit a genuine (non-EOF) I/O failure. Currently these throw a fixed generic string like "AutoFile::write: write failed" that discards the OS-level reason. The PR adds a test asserting the OS error is now present, and the author already fixed a musl-CI test failure by switching the failure-forcing technique to a genuine kernel EBADF rather than a libc-internal precheck.
result.problem: AutoFile/BufferedFile exception messages discard the errno explaining why an fread/fwrite call failed, so any caller (including logs or user-facing errors) that surfaces e.what() loses diagnostic detail. This was noticed while reviewing #35492, which will want to surface this detail when a wallet dump aborts.

resolved_concerns: musl CI failure due to test relying on a libc-internal precheck that doesn't set errno; author reworked the test to force a genuine kernel-level EBADF, confirmed fixed.

result.card: This PR makes AutoFile and BufferedFile I/O failure exceptions include the OS errno/strerror detail instead of a fixed generic string, so callers that log or surface e.what() get the real reason a read/write failed. It originated from review of #35492 (wallet dump abort on incomplete writes), which will want to surface this detail once its dump.cpp rework lands. The author already fixed an Alpine/musl CI failure by reworking the test to force a genuine kernel-level EBADF rather than relying on a libc-internal precheck that musl doesn't set errno for. No reviewers have commented on the substance yet. The change is a diagnostics improvement, not a correctness or security fix, and nothing is known to block review right now.
